clue.text: Crazy time to go round islands in the North Atlantic

parts.note: crazy means mad

indicators.note: the word for time goes round, enclosing the islands letter

parts.note: an era is a period of time
I or Is is the map abbreviation for island(s)

explanation.surface: A wild spell of sailing around the islands of the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer names the archipelago that lies in the North Atlantic, so 'islands' does duty in the surface as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island group lying out in the North Atlantic off Morocco.

clue.text: Scholar liable to drift

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
under means subject or liable to, as in under suspicion

explanation.surface: An academic who tends to wander off course.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to ramble or wander aimlessly, in speech or movement.

clue.text: Student put out by deviation and apostasy

indicators.note: the learner letter is ejected from the word for deviation

parts.note: deflection is a turning aside, a deviation
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A pupil upset by heresy and betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out by' removes L from DEFLECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is abandoning one's faith or cause, a desertion to the other side.

clue.text: Stress present in a 5ac tussle

annotationWithheld.why: Stress present in a 5ac tussle (5): hidden in 'a HOMERIC tussle' via the cross-reference to 5 across; the checker reads the printed clue letters only, where '5ac' does not supply HOMERIC, so the hidden run cannot be shown.

clue.text: Relating to a legendary king badly hurt in an air crash

indicators.note: an air crash smashes things up, so these letters are shattered and remade
something badly hurt is mangled, suggesting the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A mythical monarch is seriously injured in a plane accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles HURT, and 'crash' then shuffles those letters with AN AIR; 'in' merely links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian describes the legends of King Arthur and the Round Table.

clue.text: Imposing house concealed crime

indicators.note: the word crime is disguised, its letters reworked so it cannot be recognised

explanation.surface: A grand mansion hid a criminal secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' is an unusual anagram signal: a disguised crime has its letters hidden in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means on an epic, heroic scale, like the poems of Homer, hence grand and impressive.

clue.text: Cache put by for the gang, say

indicators.note: this word signals that the gang word is spoken, giving a same-sounding one

parts.note: a horde is a large gang or crowd

explanation.surface: A stash stored away for the criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stock of valuables stored away secretly.

clue.text: It needs a screw to keep it going

definitions.text: It needs a screw to keep it going

parts.words: It needs a screw to keep it going
parts.note: sounds like a mechanical gadget held together, but a screw here is a ship's propeller driving a small powered craft

explanation.definitionFit: A powered boat is driven through water by its propeller, commonly called a screw.

clue.text: Country source of Russian river

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Ural is a river of Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A nation where a Russian river rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural, as in the country, describes the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Copper about to feel aversion for a castle

indicators.note: the copper letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to hate is to feel aversion

explanation.surface: A policeman about to take a dislike to a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman in the surface, but here it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Not suitable to keep a filly in one

indicators.note: the filly letter is placed in the word for one

parts.note: a unit is a single one
F is the abbreviation for filly in racing form

explanation.surface: A remark that a young mare is out of place among the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit and not suitable are synonyms, describing something inappropriate for a purpose.

clue.text: Publicize rejection returning pie to restaurant

annotationWithheld.why: Publicize rejection by returning pie to restaurant (9): TART reversed gives TRAT, but no reading found that makes the remaining TORIA from 'Publicize rejection by'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Publicize rejection returning pie to restaurant

clue.text: Theologian crosses a church to avoid a dog

indicators.note: the two letters for the theologian stretch across, enclosing the rest

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
to shun is to avoid

explanation.surface: A clergyman cuts across a churchyard to dodge a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a degree held by theologians.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund is a long-bodied, short-legged breed of German hound.

clue.text: Italian king accommodating family of Austro-German poet

indicators.note: the word for king houses the word for family inside it

parts.note: re is Italian for king
ilk means kind or family

explanation.surface: A monarch of Italy hosting a poet's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Re is Italian for king; the poet is Rainer Maria Rilke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke, born in Prague, wrote German-language lyric poetry such as the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Controls — and wears the crown, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for ruling as monarch is said out loud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a monarch who wears the crown reigns

explanation.surface: A ruler both governs and wears the regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps for steering a horse, and figuratively the means of control.

clue.text: Plant and much money accumulated for future use

parts.note: stock is a garden flowering plant
a pile is a fortune, a lot of money

explanation.surface: A garden flower and a fortune saved up for later.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a noun phrase: (what is) accumulated for future use.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile is a reserve built up against later need.

clue.text: Spontaneous claim to be employed by theatre and university

parts.note: saying I'm so-and-so is claiming to be it
a prompt is the cue given to actors in a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone casually says they work for a theatre and a college.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu remark is unplanned, made on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Dance madly — peter out about one

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the one
madly means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone dances frantically, then the energy fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges PETER OUT and 'about' places it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot, a ballet movement.

clue.text: Endlessly courteous hanger-on — no executive

indicators.note: the word for courteous loses its final letter

parts.note: polite means courteous
a bur is a clinging seed head, so a hanger-on
O, nought, means none

explanation.surface: A courteous parasite with no authority.
explanation.walkthrough: A bur (or burr) clings to clothing, hence a hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of a Communist party.

clue.text: Poet accepting directions from the laird, perhaps

indicators.note: the poet's name takes the compass letters inside it

parts.note: Walter Savage Landor was an English poet
W, N and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: A poet takes orders from the Scottish lord of the manor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts W, N, E inside LANDOR. A laird is a Scottish estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird holds a Scottish estate, so he is an example of someone who owns property.

clue.text: Way without sink to make pasta

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the way word is around the sink word

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: A recipe made without a kitchen basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is flat sheets of pasta, often baked in layers.

clue.text: They're often told, thanks to the French

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Things often said, with gratitude to France.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are things that get told, as in telling tales.

clue.text: The picturesque view of the theatre?

definitions.text: The picturesque view of the theatre?

parts.words: The picturesque view of the theatre?
parts.note: a pretty view and the painted backdrops on a theatre stage share one word

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both natural landscape and a stage's painted sets.

clue.text: Flighty type supposedly delivering the latest issue

definitions.text: Flighty type supposedly delivering the latest issue

parts.words: Flighty type supposedly delivering the latest issue
parts.note: reads like a frivolous newsagent with the newest edition, but describes the bird of folklore that flies in newborn babies, issue meaning offspring

explanation.definitionFit: Legend says this long-legged bird brings new babies, the latest issue of a family.

clue.text: He's immature — and he doesn't give a hoot!

definitions.text: He's immature — and he doesn't give a hoot!

parts.words: He's immature — and he doesn't give a hoot!
parts.note: sounds like a careless youth, but a very young bird of prey is too young to hoot

explanation.definitionFit: A young nocturnal bird, too young yet to give its call.

clue.text: Pert maid in "Our Betters" runs off in disarray

indicators.note: the remaining letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
the runs letter goes off, removed from the play title

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cheeky servant in a Maugham play flees in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' takes one R from OURBETTERS; 'in disarray' rearranges the rest. Our Betters is a Somerset Maugham comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is the stock role of a coquettish lady's maid in comedy or opera.

clue.text: Begin to jump

explanation.definitionFit: To start is to commence, and also to give a sudden jerk in surprise.

clue.text: Set to receive notice in port?

indicators.note: the notice letters go in the port name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A harbour expecting a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless set receives broadcasts, so a set is a receiver.

clue.text: Girl alighted out of vehicle to flirt

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

indicators.note: the word for alighted sits outside the vehicle word

parts.note: lit is a past form of alight, as a bird lights on a branch
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A young woman steps out of a car to chat someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' here means outside, wrapping around, not leaving; the flirting sense of the answer is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of gallivant is to gad about flirting with the opposite sex.

clue.text: It's the devil of a score!

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a terrible result.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is an old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the deuce', and in tennis a forty-all score.

clue.text: Ask soldiers to enter a tent, perhaps

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters go into the shuffled tent letters
the letters of a tent are taken as one possible arrangement among others

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Inviting troops into a canvas shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A TENT to ENTAT; 'to enter' puts RE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly with someone.

clue.text: County dividing money produced by retrenchment

indicators.note: the county letters split the other letters into two parts
the letters of money are brought forth in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A council splitting the funds it raised by cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a loose anagram signal: the money letters are brought out in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrenchment means cutting spending, which is making savings.
